2607.09520.title: Seeing is Free, Speaking is Not: Uncovering the True Energy Bottleneck in Edge VLM Inference
2607.09520.paper_summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are the perceptual backbone of embodied AI, but their energy footprint on edge hardware remains poorly understood. Existing efficiency efforts focus predominantly on reducing visual tokens, implicitly treating visual processing as the dominant energy cost. We overturn this implicit assumption through the first systematic energy profiling of on-device VLM inference, spanning five models across three architecture families, four input resolutions, and two hardware platforms (NVIDIA RTX 3070 and Jetson Orin NX). Our analysis yields three findings. First, average inference power is a model-intrinsic constant, invariant to input resolution, image complexity, and prompt type, with less than 5% variation across all conditions. This means that all energy variation across inputs must arise from variation in inference time, not from variation in power draw. Second, each output token costs 11 to 39x more wall-clock time than each input token due to the compute-bound and memory-bound asymmetry between prefill and decode, making output token count the dominant driver of both latency and energy. Third, image complexity, measured by the number of objects in an image, induces up to 4.1x energy differences at identical resolution. This variation arises not from increased visual processing cost, but from differences in output length. These findings expose a fundamental limitation of visual token pruning: even removing all visual tokens saves at most 10% of total energy for fixed-token models. Across models spanning 1 billion to 8 billion parameters, controlling output length saves up to 97% of total energy, with the energy dominance of decoding growing stronger at larger model scale. In short, the true energy bottleneck in edge VLM inference is not what the model sees, but how much it says.
2607.09520.paper_summary_zh: 視覺-語言模型 (VLMs) 是具身 AI 的感知基礎，但它們在邊緣硬體上的能量足跡仍然不甚了解。現有的效率努力主要集中在減少視覺標記，隱含地將視覺處理視為主要的能量成本。我們通過對在設備上進行 VLM 推理的首次系統性能量分析推翻了這一隱含假設，涵蓋了三個架構系列中的五個模型、四個輸入解析度和兩個硬體平台（NVIDIA RTX 3070 和 Jetson Orin NX）。我們的分析得出了三個發現。首先，平均推理功率是一個模型內在的常數，與輸入解析度、圖像複雜性和提示類型無關，在所有條件下變化不到 5%。這意味著所有輸入之間的能量變化必須源於推理時間的變化，而不是功耗的變化。第二，每個輸出標記的牆鐘時間比每個輸入標記多 11 到 39 倍，這是由於預填充和解碼之間的計算限制和記憶體限制的不對稱，使得輸出標記數量成為延遲和能量的主要驅動因素。第三，圖像複雜性（通過圖像中的物體數量來衡量）在相同解析度下會引起多達 4.1 倍的能量差異。這種變化不是由於視覺處理成本的增加，而是由於輸出長度的差異。這些發現揭示了視覺標記修剪的一個基本限制：即使刪除所有視覺標記，對於固定標記模型來說，最多也只能節省 10% 的總能量。在跨越 10 億到 80 億參數的模型中，控制輸出長度可以節省多達 97% 的總能量，隨著模型規模的增大，解碼的能量主導性變得更強。簡而言之，邊緣 VLM 推理中的真正能量瓶頸不是模型所看到的，而是它所說的多少。
